subject: Error when estimating simple model - replacement has length zero (data and code attached)

messages.author: cd1835d7cf8edf1d
messages.subject: Error when estimating simple model - replacement has length zero (data and code attached)
parts:
I am taking a class that uses SPSS AMOS for SEM. Since I do not plan on using SPSS after the class is over, I'm trying to learn everything in R. I have over 7 years experience with R, but I'm just starting out with lavaan and SEM. I'd appreciate some help on this. Thanks!

Here is the model. I've attached the small dataset as well.

Here is how I've specified it in R.

mod1 <- '
  # latent variables
  # regressions
    SAT ~ Education + Income_centered
  # residual covariances
    Education ~~ Income_centered
'

mod1.s <- sem(mod1, w)


But when I run sem() I get an error:

Error in x[lavaanParTable$unco[lavaanParTable$op == "~" & lavaanParTable$unco]] <- x.beta[-1L] : 
  replacement has length zero
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In vnames(FLAT, "ov.x", warn = TRUE) :
  lavaan WARNING: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
  involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [Education Income_centered];
  Please use fixed.x=FALSE or leave them alone

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Error when estimating simple model - replacement has length zero (data and code attached)
parts:
the warning about the scale of variances relates to some odd behavior that you can see in some models when one variable in a model is on a dramatically different scale than another.  Education is not going to be on the same scale as SAT score or Income.  If you want to get rid of the message, rescale, perhaps by multiplying Education by 10.

Sometimes in structural equation models, observed variable covariances are experimental treatments or other variables that are under the researchers' control and not randomly distributed.  "Fixed-x = TRUE" accounts for this.  but not in your case, so "Fixed-x = FALSE" would be correct.

I don't know about the first message, but you might get rid of the warnings and then see how things stand.

-Ed Rigdon

On 01/31/2014 01:50 AM, Jesse Fagan wrote:

> mod1 <-'
> # latent variables
> # regressions
> SAT ~ Education + Income_centered
> # residual covariances
> Education ~~ Income_centered
> '

Ha. The first thing to 'learn' about lavaan is: there is no need to
include the variances/intercepts/covariances of exogenous variables in
the syntax. Unless you specify fixed.x=FALSE.

> Error in x[lavaanParTable$unco[lavaanParTable$op == "~" & lavaanParTable$unco]] <- x.beta[-1L] :
> replacement has length zero

This is an ugly uninformative error. Will fix this.

Yves.
